If Log4Shell was Java’s nightmare in 2021, then today’s disclosure of CVE‑2025‑55182 (Next.js counterpart CVE‑2025‑66478) marks the darkest hour of the modern React/Next.js full‑stack era.
A CVSS score of 10.0, unauthenticated RCE, and impact across React 19, Next.js 15/16, and any framework implementing React Server Components (RSC).
If you're reading this before coffee:

drop everything and check your versions.
React’s core team has officially confirmed a critical remote code execution vulnerability inside the implementation of React Server Components — and it’s as bad as it sounds.
To understand the issue, we need to understand how RSC moves data.
React Server Components rely on a streaming, JSON‑like protocol called Flight…
articles.title: CVSS 10.0 RCE Rocks the Frontend World: React/Next.js Hit by a Log4Shell‑Level Vulnerability?

articles.author: Saniya Mohammad
articles.description:
Participating in the 5-Day AI Agents Intensive was a transformative experience for me. Before joining, I had only a basic understanding of how AI systems work. But through the intensive, I learned how modern AI agents are designed, how they interact with tools, and how they solve real-world tasks in an autonomous way.


One of the biggest takeaways for me was understanding how agents plan, reason, and take actions instead of just answering questions. Concepts like tool use, chaining tasks, prompt design, and structured reasoning helped me clearly see how powerful AI can be when combined with the right workflows. The practical exercises made everything feel real and approachable. 


I especially enjoyed working with Kaggle’s notebook environment, experimenting with prompts, and seeing how small prompt changes influenced an agent’s performance. It was exciting to watch an AI system break down a complex problem into steps and generate meaningful outputs.


Another important learning was the importance of evaluation, safety, and reliability. I understood that building an agent is not just about making it “work,” but making it predictable, responsible, and aligned with user goals. This gave me a more professional perspective on AI development.



5.Overall, this intensive boosted my confidence and motivation to learn further. I now feel comfortable exploring advanced topics like workflow automation, model fine-tuning, and end-to-end agent design. I’m grateful to the Kaggle community and instructors for creating such an interactive learning experience.
6.This journey inspired me to continue building my skills, contribute to real-world AI projects, and keep learning through Kaggle courses.
Thank you for this opportunity!
articles.title: ⭐ My AI Agents Intensive Learning Journey – Challenge Submission
